chapter: After the Paradise: club dates and Virginia
title: Leaving the Paradise in 1952, then the Hotel America's Bamboo Room
summary: Entertainment was curtailed after the club's Ebony write-up and money problems; he took a job in the Bamboo Room at the Hotel America.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So, just to return to the Paradise and the general historical progression here. You left the Paradise in 1952 was it?

Well, the place...the corner got so hot and so popular and we got a write up in a national magazine (Ebony) and what not. Things...I don't know...something happened internally and I don't know exactly what happened, but they decided to curtail the entertainment for a cooling off period. I don't know what happened internally, but anyway that's what happened there. So I had to keep workin', you know, I had that house. So I went down town.
I'm just curious--just to stop you for a second--how did that come down, who told you that and what...

you know, they told me that things had gotten out of hand; I don't know what it was, something internal, I don't know. There was so many people involved, you know. There was so much money being made and the funds were missing and things like that, you know. And things got a little warm there. So, I had another job to go to. I went down to the Hotel America which was on...I think it was 48th Street. They had a room there called the Bamboo Room and a lot of musicians stayed downtown, some of Duke's men. Paul stayed there when he was in town and Jimmy Grissom and James Edwards, the actor, and Leontyne Price when she was married to William Warfield, at the time. And so I had something there for about a year and a half. But before I left the Paradise, Timmy said, "Look here, I'm gonna get you out of this corner. Why don't you come on with me." So I heard him, you know. You know I been knowin' Timmy 'cause he...in fact he did several weeks down there at the Cafe Society when I was with J.C. Heard. He was one of the stars.
